rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains al-Ṣamad and rejects attributing offspring or lineage to God, including Christian claims about Jesus and polytheist claims about angels.
rows.anchor: Allah’a evlât nisbet edenleri ve soy kavramına giren her şeyi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having children entails a spouse; both arise from desires to meet needs, whereas God is need-free and cannot need what He created.
rows.anchor: Çocuk, eşin olmasını gerektirir; eş de çocuk da bazı ihtiyaçları karşılama arzu ve eğiliminin sonuçlarıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause means God did not originate through birth or emanation from a parent or source; everything born is subsequent, but God is eternal and beginningless.
rows.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın doğum veya sudûr yoluyla bir ana veya babadan, bir asıldan meydana gelmediğini ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no equal or likeness in essence, attributes, or acts; this verse explains the opening verse and summarizes the surah, glossing its declaration of oneness.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın zâtında, sıfatlarında ve fiillerinde denksiz ve benzersiz olduğu şeklindeki anlamıyla ilk âyetteki “ahad”ın tefsiri gibidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God created everything besides Himself, none of His creations can be His equal.
rows.anchor: Kendisinden başka var olan her şeyi O yarattığına göre yarattıklarının O’na denk olması mümkün değildir

rows.speaker: âlimlerden bir kısmı
rows.claim: Some scholars interpret the surah's equivalence to one third of the Qur'an as equivalence in the reward for reciting it.
rows.anchor: bu denkliği sûreyi okumanın sevabı

rows.speaker: âlimlerden bir kısmı
rows.claim: Other scholars interpret the equivalence by subject and meaning: the surah teaches tawhid, so understanding it means grasping the Qur'an's section on monotheism and creed.
rows.anchor: konusu ve mânası yönünden değerlendirmişlerdir. İkinci görüşe göre sûre

rows.speaker: Gazzâlî
rows.claim: Ghazali divides Qur'anic knowledge into knowledge of God, the afterlife, and the right path; Ikhlas contains the first, and other rulings rest on its tawhid foundation.
rows.anchor: Gazzâlî Cevâhiru’l-Kur’ân isimli eserinde (s. 47-48)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because of its importance, the surah has received extensive commentaries, independent studies across disciplines from philosophy to Sufism, and academic theses.
rows.anchor: felsefeden tasavvufa kadar çeşitli ilim dallarında da meşhur âlimler tarafından sûre üzerinde pek çok müstakil tefsir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falaq is a noun derived from falq, meaning to split, and describes something produced by splitting or cracking.
rows.anchor: “yarmak” anlamındaki felk (فلق)masdarından isimdir. Yarma ve çatlatma neticesinde meydana gelen şeyin sıfatı

rows.speaker: müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
rows.claim: The widespread interpretation is that falaq denotes morning light produced when God splits the darkness of night.
rows.anchor: Yaygın yoruma göre burada Allah’ın gece karanlığını yarması neticesinde meydana gelen sabah aydınlığını ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context with the next verse, falaq has the broader sense of creatures emerging from nonexistence, perhaps through an initial cosmic explosion; it includes springs, rain, plants, offspring, and all creation brought forth by God's power.
rows.anchor: bir sonraki âyetle bağlantısı dikkate alındığında kelimenin, “yokluktan yarılıp çıkan mahlûkat” şeklinde özetleyebileceğimiz daha genel bir anlam içerdiğini kabul etmek gerekir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking Esed's cited definition of falaq as truth emerging after uncertainty, 'Lord of morning' may point to God as the source of every apprehension of truth and refuge as pursuing truth.
rows.anchor: felak kelimesinin, “bir belirsizlikten (dönem) sonra hakikatin ortaya çıkışı” şeklindeki tanımı

rows.speaker: müfessirler
rows.claim: Older commentaries also identify falaq as Hell, a prison in Hell, a plant, or a well; the author considers these interpretations mistaken.
rows.anchor: “cehennemin ismi, cehennemde bir zindanın veya bitkinin ya da kuyunun ismi” gibi –bize göre isabetli olmayan– başka yorumlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge covers every kind of harm from creation: material or spiritual, worldly or otherworldly, external or inward, natural or chosen.
rows.anchor: maddî ve mânevî, dünyevî ve uhrevî, dış âlemde veya kişinin nefsinde, tabii ve ihtiyarî, her türlü şerri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although creation belongs to God, every creature has a known or unknown wisdom, benefit, and function within the divine plan.
rows.anchor: her yaratılanın aynı zamanda bizim bildiğimiz veya bilemeyeceğimiz bir hikmeti, bir faydası, ilâhî plana uygun bir fonksiyonu vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As part of the trial, humans can choose whether to desire evil and direct their will toward carrying it out.
rows.anchor: insana kötüyü isteyip istememe ve onu icra için iradesini harekete yöneltme yetisi verilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evil belongs to conscious beings' attitudes, choices, and use of things and places; they may call evil what God has not so designated.
rows.anchor: kötülük onların tavrı, tercihi, kullanma ve uygulama biçimi ve yeri ile ilgilidir

rows.speaker: müfessirler
rows.claim: Commentators have glossed ghasiq as cold, the Pleiades, sun, moon, snake, or anything harmful, implying refuge when each descends, sets, eclipses, strikes, or threatens.
rows.anchor: müfessirler “soğuk, Süreyya yıldızı, güneş, ay, yılan ve zarar veren her şey” mânalarını da vermişlerdir

rows.speaker: müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
rows.claim: Most commentators prefer the meaning 'night'; its darkness was frightening, especially in the circumstances of the revelation, and made ordinary activity and protection difficult.
rows.anchor: müfessirlerin çoğunluğu bizim meâlde verdiğimiz “gece” mânasını tercih etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi explains the command as seeking refuge from night because predators and vermin emerge, thieves attack, fires occur, and help is scarce.
rows.anchor: Râzî şöyle der: “Geceleyin yırtıcı hayvanlar inlerinden, haşereler yerlerinden çıktığı, hırsızlar ve soyguncular hücuma geçtiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collapsing darkness may also be metaphorical: injustice, ignorance, dark thoughts, destructive passions, death, despair, and pessimism that frighten or distress people.
rows.anchor: “Çöken karanlık” mecazi anlamda zulüm ve cehalet karanlığı, karanlık düşünceler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naffathat is used for both men and women, while uqad is the plural of uqda, meaning a knot.
rows.anchor: neffâsât kelimesi hem erkek hem de kadın için kullanılır

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says 'those who blow on knots' may mean female magicians, magicians generally, or groups of magicians.
rows.anchor: “Düğümlere üfürenler” diye tercüme ettiğimiz ifade, “kadın sihirbazlar, sihirbaz insanlar, sihirbaz gruplar” anlamlarında da yorumlanmıştır

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: One possibility is seeking refuge from sorcerers' practice itself and its sin.
rows.anchor: a) Sihir ve büyü ile uğraşanların yaptıkları işten ve bunun günahından

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: A second possibility is seeking refuge from female sorcerers' efforts to mislead people into temptation and deceive them with falsehood.
rows.anchor: b) Büyücü kadınların, bu işle insanları fitneye düşürmelerinden ve bâtıl şeylerle insanları aldatmalarından

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: A third possibility is refuge from calamities God may send when sorcerers blow, rather than from the spell's own effect.
rows.anchor: c) Sihirbazlar üfürdükleri zaman onların büyülemesinden değil, Allah’tan gelebilecek musibetlerden

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi proposes a metaphor: women whose sexual allure affects men as if by magic and induces them to do various things.
rows.anchor: Râzî, neffâsât kelimesini, “cinsel cazibeleriyle erkekleri âdeta büyülercesine etkileyip türlü türlü işler yaptıran kadınlar”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prevalent interpretation is actual male and female sorcerers and charmers; believers are commanded to seek refuge from their evil.
rows.anchor: yaygın yoruma göre burada gerçek büyücü ve üfürükçüler kastedilmiş ve kadınıyla erkeğiyle büyü ile meşgul olan herkesin şerrinden Allah’a sığınılması emredilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic practice, magic could be performed by tying a cord, reciting words over its knots, and blowing on them.
rows.anchor: Câhiliye döneminde ipi düğümleyerek ve düğümlere bir şeyler okuyup üfleyerek büyü yapıldığı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names practitioners' evil, not the magical effect of blowing on a knotted cord; such people deceive and confuse others and divert them from truth and sound measures toward mistaken conduct.
rows.anchor: Âyette düğümlü ipe üflenerek yapılan büyünün etkisinden ve şerrinden değil, bunu yapanların kötülüğünden söz edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also shows believers should not trust, honor, or value magicians and charmers, but should stay away from them.
rows.anchor: müminlerin büyücü ve üfürükçülere itibar etmemeleri, onlardan uzak durmaları, onlara değer vermekten sakınmaları gerektiğini

rows.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri warned, when this verse was discussed, to beware of people involved in magic.
rows.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî, bu âyet söz konusu olduğunda “Sihre bulaşanlardan sakının” demiştir

rows.speaker: müfessirler
rows.claim: Commentators who regard the surahs as Medinan cite reports that a Jew bewitched the Prophet, who was ill for six months or longer and imagined saying or doing things; the two surahs then came and healed him.
rows.anchor: Felak ve Nâs sûrelerinin Medine’de indiğini söyleyen müfessirler burada bir yahudi tarafından Hz. Peygamber’e sihir yapıldığını

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Like other Mu'tazilites, Zamakhshari rejects belief in the reality and effects of such magical practices.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî de âyetle ilgili yorumunda, bu tür uygulamaların gerçekliğine ve etkilerine inanmayı kesinlikle reddeder

rows.speaker: Muhammed Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh rejects the reports as conflicting with verses that say the Prophet and revelation are protected from magic and similar human influences.
rows.anchor: Muhammed Abduh, böyle bir olayın peygamberin ve vahyin sihir vb. beşerî etkilerden korunmuşluğunu ifade eden âyetlere

rows.speaker: Reşîd Rızâ
rows.claim: Rashid Rida presents a similar objection in greater detail, also drawing on psychological findings.
rows.anchor: Benzer görüş Reşîd Rızâ tarafından –mevcut psikolojik bulgulara da dayanılarak– daha ayrıntılı bir şekilde ifade edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says many Sunni scholars agree that non-mutawatir reports cannot ground matters of knowledge and belief; such reports about the Prophet's alleged bewitching should therefore not be accepted.
rows.anchor: bilgi ve inanç konularında mütevâtir olmayan rivayetlerin dayanak olamayacağı birçok Sünnî âlimin üzerinde birleştiği bir kural olup

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hasid is an adjective from hased, envy; it describes someone affected by envy and resentment, the desire for another's blessing to disappear.
rows.anchor: hâsid kelimesi “kıskanmak” anlamına gelen hased kökünden sıfat olup kıskançlık ve çekememezlik duygusunun tesirinde kalan kişiyi ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islamic ethical works count envy among the principal sources of evil.
rows.anchor: İslâm ahlâk kaynaklarında başlıca kötülük sebepleri arasında gösterilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Envy is treated as a spiritual illness rooted in selfishness and inability to tolerate another's advantage, causing distress.
rows.anchor: insan tabiatındaki bencillik eğiliminden, dolayısıyla başkalarının kendisinden daha üstün durumda olmasına tahammül edememesinden kaynaklandığı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse stresses seeking God's protection from an envious person when the envy takes hold.
rows.anchor: kıskançlığı tutan hasetçinin şerrinden Allah’a sığınmanın önemine dikkat çekilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is called Rabb because He creates people and nourishes, develops, and educates them physically and spiritually through His blessings.
rows.anchor: insanları yaratıp maddî ve mânevî nimetleriyle hem bedenen hem de ruhen beslediği, yetiştirdiği, eğittiği için

rows.speaker: Râgıb el-İsfahânî
rows.claim: Raghib explains malik as one who governs a human community through commands and prohibitions; the term is used for rulers of rational beings, not things.
rows.anchor: Râgıb el-İsfahânî, “mâlik ve hâkim” diye çevirdiğimiz 2. âyetteki melik kelimesini özetle şöyle açıklar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since all people are under God's governance, only God is their ruler and sovereign through laws, commands, and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: Yönetilen bütün insanlar olunca kanunlarıyla, buyruk ve yasaklarıyla onların yöneticisi, mâlik ve hâkimi de Allah’tan başkası değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilah means God alone, the only one worthy of worship.
rows.anchor: “Mâbud” diye çevirdiğimiz ilâhtan maksat da sadece kendisi ibadete lâyık olan Allah’tır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating 'people' in all three verses, although God is Lord of all creation, signals that humanity is the highest and noblest creation.
rows.anchor: burada üç âyette de, “insanlar”ın tekrarlanarak vurgulanması, onların mahlûkatın en üstünü ve en şereflisi olduğuna işarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because human rulers and peoples who deified them have existed and still exist in varied forms, the surah insists that God alone is humanity's Lord, ruler, and deity, and alone should be worshipped and sought for refuge.
rows.anchor: insanların rablerinin de, hükümdarlarının da, ilâhlarının da sadece Allah olduğuna ve yalnızca O’na sığınmak, O’na tapmak, O’nun hükümranlığını tanımak gerektiğine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswas is an intensive form from whispering, meaning one who whispers often; whispering may mean doubt, hesitation, fantasy, concealed speech, or inward thought.
rows.anchor: vesveseden türemiş, aşırılık ifade eden bir sıfat olup “çokça vesvese veren” demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Technically, whispering is an involuntary, obscurely sourced thought or doubt arising in the mind and steering someone toward bad or useless thought and conduct.
rows.anchor: zihinde irade dışı beliren ve kişiyi kötü ya da faydasız bir düşünce ve davranışa sürükleyen kaynağı belirsiz fikir, şüphe ve kuruntu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whispering is generally felt as an inner urge toward bad, religiously or ethically improper conduct, and its source is Satan.
rows.anchor: Vesvese genel olarak insanı kötü, din ve ahlâk dışı davranışlara yönelten bir iç itilme olarak hissedilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many verses say Satan whispers to people.
rows.anchor: birçok âyette şeytanın insana vesvese verdiği ifade edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is a real being, but his influence on people is thought to operate psychologically.
rows.anchor: Kötülük sembolü olan şeytan, gerçek bir varlığa sahip olmakla birlikte onun insan üzerindeki etkisini psikolojik yolla gerçekleştirdiği düşünülmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second source of whispering is the self, as Qaf 50:16 indicates.
rows.anchor: Vesvesenin bir diğer kaynağı ise kişinin nefsidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswas can denote both the unseen Satan who whispers to people and human devils who secretly plot to lead them astray and make them do evil.
rows.anchor: Vesvâs kelimesi hem insanlara vesvese veren görünmez şeytanı hem de insanları yoldan çıkarmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khannas means one who acts secretly and habitually stays behind or recedes.
rows.anchor: “gizli hareket eden ve geride kalmayı âdet haline getiren” anlamında bir sıfattır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek refuge from jinn and human evil also calls for vigilance about unclear or inward desires and thoughts, testing them against reason, conscience, and religious values.
rows.anchor: bunları akıl, vicdan ve dinî değerler süzgecinden geçirmeyi de içermektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final verse identifies two kinds of devils: jinn who whisper and try to mislead people, each person having a jinn that makes bad acts seem attractive.
rows.anchor: Birincisi cin şeytanlarıdır ki bunlar insanların içine vesvese düşürerek onları yanlış yola sürüklemek isterler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet said that every person has a jinn or devil of his own.
rows.anchor: Hz. Peygamber, her insanın kendine ait bir cini (şeytanı) bulunduğunu bildirmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another hadith says Satan moves through the veins of Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: “Şeytan âdemoğlunun kan damarlarında dolaşır” buyurulur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other devils are people who have lost truth and value standards, surrendered to selfish desires, corrupted their pure nature, and become advocates of evil like unseen devils.
rows.anchor: Bunlar, gerçeklik ve değer ölçülerini kaybetmiş, kendilerini nefsânî haz ve arzuların akıntısına kaptırmış

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: When God described what is in Paradise, the people of misguidance were amazed; then the verse directing them to consider how camels were created was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال لما نعت الله ما في الجنة عجب من ذلك أهل الضلالة فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet was shown what would be opened to his community after him and rejoiced, so the statement that the Hereafter is better than the first life was revealed; al-Tabarani's chain is graded good.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عرض علي ما هو مفتوح لأمتي بعدي فسرني فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet was shown the conquests opening for his community village by village and rejoiced; then the promise of God's giving until he is satisfied was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال عرض على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما هو مفتوح على أمته كفرا كفرا أي قرية قرية فسر به

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Hasan ibn Ali reports that the Prophet saw Umayya ibn Khalaf on his pulpit and was distressed; the reports connect this with Surahs 108 and 97, saying Umayyads would rule a thousand months. Tirmidhi calls it rare; al-Muzani and Ibn Kathir call it very objectionable.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي قال إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى بي أمية على منبره فساءه ذلك فنزلت

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The Prophet mentioned an Israelite who wore armor in God's path for a thousand months; Muslims marveled, and the surah was revealed, declaring Laylat al-Qadr better than those months.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر رجلا من بني إسرائيل لبس السلاح في سبيل الله ألف شهر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: An Israelite worshipped through each night and fought the enemy by day for a thousand months; the verse that Laylat al-Qadr is better was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال كان في بني إسرائيل رجل يقوم الليل حتى يصبح ثم يجاهد العدو بالنهار حتى يمسي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: After the food-giving verse, some Muslims thought small charity earned no reward, while others thought minor sins such as lying, glances, and backbiting were not blameworthy; these verses addressed both views.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال لما نزلت ﴿ ويطعمون الطعام على حبه ﴾ الآية كان المسلمون يرون

rows.speaker: عثمان وابن عمر
rows.claim: Uthman and Ibn Umar said they had long heard that the threat against every backbiter and slanderer was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: عن عثمان وابن عمر قالا ما زلنا نسمع أن ﴿ ويل لكل همزة ﴾ نزلت في أبي بن خلف

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq.
rows.anchor: عن السدي قال نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق

rows.speaker: رجل من أهل الرقة
rows.claim: A man from al-Raqqa says the verse was revealed about Jamil ibn Amir al-Jumahi.
rows.anchor: عن رجل من أهل الرقة قال نزلت في جميل بن عامر الجمحي

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Umayya ibn Khalaf used to mock and slander the Prophet when he saw him, so the whole surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق قال كان أمية بن خلف إذا

rows.speaker: أم هانىء بنت أبي طالب
rows.claim: Umm Hani reports a hadith about seven distinctions God granted Quraysh, including a surah that mentions no people other than them, revealed concerning Quraysh.
rows.anchor: عن أم هانىء بنت أبي طالب قالت قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فضل الله قريشا بسبع خصال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the threatened worshippers were hypocrites who performed prayer ostentatiously when believers saw them, abandoned it when unseen, and withheld borrowed household goods.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله ﴿ فويل للمصلين ﴾ الآية قال نزلت في المنافقين كانوا يراؤون المؤمنين بصلاتهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf visited Mecca, Quraysh asked whether he saw their leader Muhammad cut off from his people; Ka'b said they were better, and the verse answered them. The report's chain is sound.
rows.anchor: بسند صحيح عن ابن عباس قال قدم كعب ابن الأشرف مكة فقالت له قريش أنت سيدهم ألا ترى إلى هذا المنصبر المنبتر

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says Quraysh called Muhammad cut off from them after revelation came to him, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة قال لما أوحي إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت قريش بتر محمد منا فنزلت

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Quraysh called a man cut off when his sons died; after the Prophet's son died, al-As ibn Wa'il called Muhammad cut off, and the verse followed. Another report identifies the son as al-Qasim.
rows.anchor: عن السدي قال كانت قريش تقول إذا مات ذكور الرجل بتر فلان فلما مات ولد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the verse was revealed about al-As ibn Wa'il, who declared himself Muhammad's hater.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال نزلت في العاصي بن وائل وذلك أنه قال أنا شانىء محمد

rows.speaker: أبو أيوب
rows.claim: A weak report says that when Ibrahim, the Prophet's son, died, polytheists said the 'Ṣābiʾ' had been cut off that night, and the whole surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن أبي أيوب قال لما مات إبراهيم ابن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مشى المشركون بعضهم إلى بعض

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the command to pray and sacrifice came at Hudaybiya: Gabriel instructed the Prophet, who preached, prayed two units, and sacrificed camels; al-Suyuti calls the report extremely strange.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله ﴿ فصل لربك وانحر ﴾ قال نزلت يوم الحديبية

rows.speaker: شمر بن عطية
rows.claim: Shamir ibn Atiyya says Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt predicted the Prophet would have no surviving son and be cut off, so the verse was revealed about him.
rows.anchor: عن شمر بن عطية قال كان عقبة بن أبي معيط يقول إنه لا يبقى للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولد وهو أبتر

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says that when the Prophet's son Ibrahim died, Quraysh called Muhammad cut off; his grief led to the consolation that God had given him al-Kawthar.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال بلغني أن إبراهيم ولد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما مات قالت قريش أصبح محمد أبتر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Quraysh offered the Prophet wealth and marriage if he stopped criticizing their idols, otherwise proposed worshipping their gods for a year; after awaiting revelation, he received this surah and 39:64.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن قريشا دعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى أن يعطوه مالا فيكون أغنى رجل بمكة

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Quraysh proposed that the Prophet follow their religion for a year and they would return to his religion the next year; the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن وهب قال قالت كفار قريش للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن سرك أن تتبعنا عاما ونرجع إلى دينك عاما

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj also reported a version of the alternating-year proposal.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج

rows.speaker: سعيد بن ميناء
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Mina says al-Walid, al-As, al-Aswad, and Umayya asked Muhammad to worship what they worship and share fully in their religious practice; the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن ميناء قال لقي الوليد بن المغيرة والعاصي بن وائل والأسود بن المطلب وأمية بن خلف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reports that during the conquest of Mecca Khalid ibn al-Walid fought Quraysh in lower Mecca until they were defeated; weapons were then lifted, people entered Islam, and the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن معمر عن الزهري قال لما دخل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مكة عام الفتح بعث خالد بن الوليد فقاتل بمن معه صفوف قريش

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On Safa the Prophet called Quraysh, asked if they would believe his warning of an approaching enemy, and warned of severe punishment; Abu Lahab cursed him and the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال صعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم على الصفا فنادى يا صباحاه فاجتمعت إليه قريش

rows.speaker: يزيد بن زيد
rows.claim: A report through Ibn Ishaq says Abu Lahab's wife used to place thorns in the Prophet's path, and the surah from its opening through the verse about his wife was revealed; Ikrima reports similarly.
rows.anchor: عن رجل من همدان يقال له يزيد بن زيد أن امراة أبي ليست كانت تلقي في طريق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الشوك فنزلت

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b reports that polytheists asked the Prophet to describe God's lineage; this surah was revealed, which al-Suyuti cites as evidence it is Meccan.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب أن المشركين قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انسب لنا ربك فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jews including Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Huyayy ibn Akhtab asked the Prophet to describe his Lord; the surah was revealed, evidence for its Medinan origin.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن اليهود جاءت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم كعب بن الأشرف وحيي بن أخطب فقالوا يا محمد صف لنا ربك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the confederates asked the Prophet to describe his Lord; al-Suyuti identifies them with the polytheists in Ubayy's report, making the surah Medinan and reconciling the reports.
rows.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال قال قتادة قالت الأحزاب انسب لنا ربك

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that Jews of Khaybar asked about their Lord after describing how various creatures were created; Gabriel then brought this surah.
rows.anchor: من طريق أبان عن أنس قال أتت يهود خيبر

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most authorities say the Opening was revealed in Mecca and was among the Qur'an's earliest revelations.
rows.anchor: اختلفوا فيها فعند الأكثرين هي مكية من أوائل ما نزل من القرآن

rows.speaker: أبو ميسرة
rows.claim: Abu Maysara reports that before revelation the Prophet fled when a caller addressed him; Waraqa advised him to stay and listen, after which the call instructed him to attest to God's oneness and Muhammad's messengerhood and recite the Opening.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان إذا برز سمع مناديا

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali reports that the Opening descended in Mecca from a treasure beneath the Throne.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام قال: نزلت فاتحة الكتاب بمكة من كنز تحت العرش

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Prophet recited the basmala and the Opening in Mecca, Quraysh responded with a curse or similar insult.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قام النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بمكة فقال: {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid alone says the Opening is Medinan; al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl calls this an isolated slip against the scholarly majority.
rows.anchor: وعند مجاهد أن الفاتحة مدنية. قال الحسين بن الفضل: لكل عالم هفوة

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi argues it must be Meccan because the Meccan Hijr 15:87 calls the seven oft-repeated a gift to the Prophet; it is unreasonable to say he prayed for over a decade without the Opening.
rows.anchor: ومما يقطع به على أنها مكية قوله تعالى: {ولقد آتيناك سبعا من المثاني والقرآن العظيم} يعني: الفاتحة.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that after Ubayy recited the Opening, the Prophet said no comparable surah was revealed in the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur'an, calling it the seven oft-repeated and mighty Qur'an given to him.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وقرأ عليه أبي بن كعب أم القرآن، فقال:

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after Bilal defiled idols, his owner gave him to the polytheists, who tortured him; Abu Bakr bought his freedom with gold, but they alleged a prior debt, so the verses affirmed he acted only seeking God's face.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: إن بلالا لما أسلم ذهب إلى الأصنام فسلح عليها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet rejoiced when shown his community's future conquests, so these verses were revealed; he was promised a thousand pearl palaces in Paradise, each with its provisions of spouses and servants.
rows.anchor: علي بن عبد الله بن عباس، عن أبيه قال: رأى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ما يفتح على أمته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet regretted a request to receive other prophets' miracles; God reminded him that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, enriched him, expanded his chest, and removed his burden.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: The verses about Abu Jahl calling his assembly and God calling the guards were revealed concerning Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl tried to stop the Prophet praying, then boasted his assembly was largest; the verses followed, and Ibn Abbas says God's guards would seize him if he summoned it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يصلي، فجاء أبو جهل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that if Abu Jahl had called his assembly, God's guards would have seized him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: والله لو دعا ناديه لأخذته زبانية الله تبارك وتعالى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The Prophet mentioned an Israelite who wore armor fighting for God's cause for a thousand months; Muslims marveled, and the surah declared Laylat al-Qadr better than those months.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: ذكر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - رجلا من بني إسرائيل لبس السلاح في سبيل الله ألف شهر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr reports that when the earthquake surah was revealed, Abu Bakr wept; the Prophet said that if people did not sin, God would create another people who sin and are forgiven.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال؟ نزلت: {إذا زلزلت الأرض زلزالها}

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid reports two people: one dismissed tiny charity as worthless, and another dismissed minor sins because only major sins merited Hell; the verses encourage small good that can grow and warn that small sins can accumulate.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: نزلت في رجلين كان أحدهما يأتيه السائل فيستقل أن يعطيه الثمرة والكسرة والجوزة

rows.speaker: أم هانئ بنت أبي طالب
rows.claim: The surah concerns Quraysh and God's favors to them; the Prophet lists seven distinctions: caliphate, Kaaba guardianship, water provision, prophethood, victory over the Elephant, exclusive worship of God for seven years, and a surah naming only them.
rows.anchor: عن جدته أم هانئ بنت أبي طالب قالت: قال النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Kalbi say the opening about one who denies Judgment and repulses the orphan was revealed about al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل والكلبي: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي.

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abu Sufyan slaughtered two camels each week; when an orphan asked him for food, he struck the child with a stick, and the verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: كان أبو سفيان بن حرب ينحر كل أسبوع جزورين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-As ibn Wa'il met the Prophet at the Banu Sahm doorway, then called him cut off because his son Abdullah had died; Arabs called a man without a son cut off, and the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في العاص بن وائل، وذلك أنه رأى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يخرج

rows.speaker: يزيد بن رومان
rows.claim: Yazid ibn Ruman reports that al-As ibn Wa'il called the Prophet childless and said his memory would end with his death; the surah was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: حدثني يزيد بن رومان قال: كان العاص بن وائل السهمي إذا ذكر رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports al-As ibn Wa'il said he detested Muhammad and called him cut off; God answered that the Prophet's hater would be cut off from the good of this world and the next.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: كان العاص بن وائل يمر بمحمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ويقول:

rows.speaker: رهط من قريش
rows.claim: A Quraysh group proposed alternating worship of their gods and Muhammad's God for a year each, arguing both sides could share the better religion; he refused to associate anything with God, recited the surah publicly at the Kaaba, and they despaired.
rows.anchor: نزلت في رهط من قريش قالوا: يا محمد هلم فاتبع ديننا ونتبع دينك

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi dates the surah to the Prophet's return from Hunayn and says he lived two years afterward.
rows.anchor: نزلت في منصرف النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من غزوة حنين وعاش بعد نزولها سنتين.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that on returning from Hunayn, the Prophet said to Ali and Fatima that victory had come and people were entering Islam in multitudes, then glorified God and sought forgiveness.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما أقبل رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من غزوة حنين وأنزل الله تعالى: {إذا جاء نصر الله}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet called Quraysh from Safa and asked whether they would believe his warning of an approaching enemy; when he warned of severe punishment, Abu Lahab cursed him and the surah was revealed. Al-Bukhari also transmits this account.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: صعد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ذات يوم الصفا فقال:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says the Prophet summoned the clans and said he could offer no protection or worldly share, only the call to God's oneness; Abu Lahab cursed him and the verse followed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قام رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A further Ibn Abbas account connects the revelation to 26:214: after calling his nearest kin at Safa and warning that enemy cavalry might attack, Abu Lahab cursed him and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما أنزل الله تعالى: {وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين} (1) أتى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الصفا

rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك ومقاتل
rows.claim: Qatada, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil say Jews asked what God is made of, His kind, whether He eats or drinks, and who inherited the world from Him; the surah was revealed as God's distinctive description.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة والضحاك ومقاتل: جاء ناس من اليهود إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقالوا: صف لنا ربك

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b reports polytheists asked the Prophet to describe his Lord, so the surah was revealed; he explains God did not beget or come from birth because all who are born die and are inherited, while God neither dies nor is inherited.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب: أن المشركين قالوا لرسول الله صلي اله عليه وسلم انسب لنا ربك

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy explains that God has no peer or likeness, citing 'nothing is like Him.'
rows.anchor: قال: لم يكن له شبيه ولا عدل و {ليس كمثله شيء}

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports that people asked the Prophet to describe his Lord's lineage, after which the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن جابر قال: قالوا يا رسول الله، انسب لنا ربك، فنزلت:
